## 4. An exotic homeomorphism

Let \(X\) and \(X'\) denote the exotic 4-manifolds from §2. Applying the construction from §3, we obtain an associated pair of closed, aspherical 4-manifolds \(Q(X)\) and \(Q(X')\) with covers \(D(X)\) and \(D(X')\). As a step in the direction of Theorem 1.1, we prove the following:

**Theorem 4.1.** *There is a homeomorphism \(Q(X) \to Q(X')\) that is not homotopic to any diffeomorphism.*

*Proof.* Recall that \(X'\) is obtained from \(X\) by removing the interior of the Akbulut cork \(C \subset \dot{X}\) and regluing \(C\) with a twist. The homeomorphism \(X \to X'\) constructed in the proof of Proposition 2.1(d) can be viewed as the identity away from \(\dot{C}\), where the definitions of \(X\) and \(X'\) agree. This induces a \(W\)-equivariant homeomorphism \(\tilde{f}:D(X)\to D(X')\), hence descends to a homeomorphism \(f:Q(X)\to Q(X')\).

We claim that there is no diffeomorphism \(D(X)\to D(X')\), which will imply that \(f:Q(X)\to Q(X')\) is not homotopic to any diffeomorphism. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1 Introduction
A famous question due to Jakob Nielsen [Nie32] in geometric topology is the following: can
any finite subgroup G ⊂π0hAut(Σg) be lifted to an actual continuous group action on Σg,
for Σg a closed oriented surface of genus g ≥0? This turns out to be possible, with Nielsen
settling the case of G finite cyclic, and Kerckhoff [Ker83] the general case.
In high-dimensions, asking for too direct a generalisation of Nielsen’s question inevitably
results in wrong statements as there is simply no reason why a general homotopy equivalence
h: M →M should be homotopic to any homeomorphism. However, rigidity phenomena
in the theory of closed aspherical manifolds - closed connected manifolds with contractible
universal covers - give some hope in generalising Nielsen’s and Kerckhoff’s results in this
direction. This question may thus fairly be called the “generalised Nielsen realisation problem
for aspherical manifolds” and has been investigated quite intensively, see for example [RS77;
DL03; BW08; L¨uc22; DL24].2

## 🏷️ The geometric input: a chamber with a parity obstruction

The construction starts with a collared four-dimensional Poincaré pair (P,S) whose interior homotopy type is a finite graph. An epimorphism π 1​(P)→Z defines connected cyclic covers P d​ and their boundaries S d​.

A marked filling of S d​ is a compact oriented four-manifold with this identified boundary and a homotopy equivalence to P d​ compatible with the prescribed boundary map. The marking is essential: an arbitrary manifold bounding the same three-manifold is not enough.

The source constructs these two different behaviors:

  * S 2​ has a marked filling, with a relative homotopy equivalence equal to the identity on its boundary.
  * S d​ has no marked filling for any odd d≥3.

The positive construction uses plumbing caps of two colors. Each grope body has four terminal caps arranged in two red–blue pairs. In the double cover, select red caps at one vertex and blue caps at the other. Each plumbing edge has exactly one selected endpoint, giving disjoint chosen cap sheets. The source compresses the resulting surfaces and replaces disjoint punctured S 2×S 2 neighborhoods by four-balls, retaining the specified boundary and graph homotopy type. (OpenAI, 2026)

The odd-cover obstruction has a simple combinatorial endpoint. Replace each edge of an odd cycle by five red and five blue parallel edges. A hypothetical marked filling supplies formal data to an endpoint-assignment theorem: each edge must be assigned to one endpoint, with no vertex receiving both two red and two blue edges.

At every vertex, therefore, at least one color is deficient: the vertex receives at most one edge of that color. Adjacent vertices cannot have the same deficient color, since their combined capacity would be at most two while five edges of that color join them. The deficient colors must alternate, which is impossible around an odd cycle.

The hard geometric and analytic input is the implication from a marked filling to these formal data. The endpoint theorem requires compatible edge potentials, injective vertex tangent maps, an invertible tangent-difference map, exact vanishing of each vertex potential on its formal parametrization, and exact gradient-ideal relations for every two-red/two-blue choice. It is not a theorem about arbitrary edge decorations. The source obtains those identities using marked holonomy and companion tensor-obstruction results. In its nilpotent parameter rings each individual parameter squares to zero, while products of distinct parameters remain present; discarding those products would lose the four-slot relations. This post treats that formal construction and the companion marked algebraicity theorem as inputs. (OpenAI, 2026)

### The odd-cover contradiction has an exact capacity count

Once the endpoint-assignment theorem has been obtained from the marked formal data, its combinatorial consequence is short. At each vertex choose a deficient color, one for which that vertex receives at most one edge. If adjacent vertices both chose red, they could receive at most two of the five red edges joining them. Yet all five edges must be assigned to one of those two endpoints. The same argument applies to blue. Thus any choice of deficient colors must alternate along the cycle, contradicting odd length.

This separates the elementary obstruction from its difficult premise. It is the exact four-slot identities and nondegeneracy conditions of the formal construction that force an endpoint assignment. The parity argument is not an obstruction for arbitrary decorated graphs or arbitrary fillings without the specified marking.
